node.title: High-direction-distance residual charts have at most N squared rays
node.statement: Let H_U:F^U->F^R have kernel K, put N=|U|, and let d_U(y1) be the minimum weight of a lift of the nonzero syndrome direction y1. If every slope in Z on y0+gamma y1 has a lift of weight at most t in U and (N-t)^2>N(N-d_U(y1)), then |Z|<=floor(N(d_U(y1)-t)/((N-t)^2-N(N-d_U(y1))))<=N^2. Proof: the selected slopes give distinct words of K+<b1> inside one radius-t Hamming ball; agreement-set second moments pay them. Failure of the inequality gives an explicit sparse-direction lift and is the exact complementary branch. This is a fixed-chart theorem and does not aggregate charts.
